preconditions.description: The number of queries q is an integer between 1 and 150,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(n, int) and 2 <= n <= 300000 for n in query_sizes)
preconditions.description: For each query, the number of vertices n is an integer between 2 and 300,000 inclusive.
The sum of n over all queries does not exceed 300,000.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x <= n and 1 <= y <= n and x != y for (x, y) in all_edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge connects two distinct vertices with labels between 1 and n.

preconditions.expression: all(len(edges) == n - 1 for n, edges in zip(query_sizes, query_edges))
preconditions.description: Each query provides exactly n-1 edges, forming a tree structure.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly q lines, one for each query.

postconditions.expression: all(isinstance(int(line), int) and 1 <= int(line) <= n for line, n in zip(output_lines, query_sizes))
postconditions.description: Each output line is an integer representing the maximum size of a good subtree, bounded by the number of vertices in that query.

postconditions.expression: all(max_good_subtree_size(edges) == int(line) for line, edges in zip(output_lines, query_edges))
postconditions.description: For each query, the output integer equals the maximum size of a subtree that can be represented as an intersection graph of one-dimensional segments.
